fit: injected Perilla constituents and conditioned defensive behavior
assessment: Original abstract reports dose-specific direction in defensive freezing and unchanged spontaneous movement at active doses. It measures a rodent fear proxy after isolated compound injection. The earlier forced-swim experiment and later review are separate reports.

fit: solid lipid curcumin and healthy older adult digit vigilance
assessment: One-hour accuracy comparison p=.046, demographic-adjusted p=.168. The difference was no longer apparent at three hours.

fit: posted aggregate MCCB results in the Wynn oral curcumin trial
assessment: Official results give composite changes, with no separate attention-domain estimate. Registry and Wynn article describe one cohort.

fit: same cohort as terminated NCT02476708 with attention/vigilance measured
assessment: Original Table 1 reports mean changes +9.20 versus −6.80, five per arm and p=.209. Reported preparation and active dose differ from the official registry capsule regimen.

fit: oral Theracurmin versus placebo and a secondary timed attention proxy
assessment: Trail A time fell from 32.6 to 24.9 seconds versus 30.5 to 28.4 in nondemented adults (interaction p=.04). The formulation and timed task do not isolate a culinary effect on Parkinson attention.

fit: twice assessed Flanker inhibition and attention in healthy adults
assessment: Table 3 shows identical rounded trajectories for both groups (8.3 to 8.5, interaction p=.97). The comparison provides a counterweight to isolated positive supplement findings.

fit: BCM-95 turmeric formulation and repeated cognition tasks outside Parkinson disease
assessment: Original analyses show no clear attention-containing task change between arms and an inconclusive baseline to 12-month MoCA interaction (p=.25).

fit: oral phospholipid curcumin in a nonrandomized Parkinson cohort
assessment: Full tables report total NMSS without a separate attention result. MMSE was a screening criterion.

fit: nanomicellar oral curcumin randomized in Parkinson disease
assessment: Primary abstract and registry do not give an attention item or distinct attention contrast. Original full results remain open.

fit: corn oil vehicle shared by both estradiol comparison arms in rats
assessment: The author abstract attributes odor discrimination and recovery differences to the estradiol comparison on a common injection background.

fit: corn oil preference by mouse olfactory-model status
assessment: Experimentally altered olfaction preceded the oil-choice task. Normal mice preferred a wider concentration range. The study does not estimate smell changes after oil intake.

fit: corn oil injection sham in mouse olfactory training
assessment: The reported pellet-finding times separate injury and training arms from an injected sham. No oil-only dietary comparison.

fit: oat bran comparator with cognition measurements
assessment: Official protocol lists oat bran powder and a different active comparator. No posted results, cooked whole oats or separate hand dexterity test.

fit: carrot frequency model and independent rhinitis-olfaction model
assessment: The carrot odds-ratio text is inconsistent, and the separate rhinitis-to-smell association does not establish a carrot effect. Preparation, temporality and Parkinson applicability remain unresolved.
